title: Asking a close friend for a favor
situation: Your phone is about to die and you forgot your charger. You text a close friend to borrow theirs, ask for yesterday's class notes, and sheepishly borrow a little cash for the bus.
tip: With close friends, open with 부탁이 있는데 to flag the request, then soften with 미안한데 + a ~줄 수 있어? question. 반말 plus a casual 좀 makes it feel light, not demanding.

turns.en: Oh hey, what's up? Something going on?

turns.prompt: Flag that you have a favor to ask before getting into it.

choices.ko: 어 부탁이 있는데… 들어줄 수 있어?
choices.en: Hey, I've got a favor to ask… could you do it for me?
choices.feedback: 부탁이 있는데 prepares your friend before the request, and -줄 수 있어? asks without sounding demanding.

choices.en: Do what I'm asking. (sounds like an order)
choices.feedback: The command 들어 leaves your friend no room to respond and sounds demanding.

choices.en: Might I trouble you for a favor? (too formal for a close friend)
choices.feedback: 드려도 될까요 is polite and useful elsewhere, but it is too formal for this close-friend text.

turns.en: Sure, go ahead, what is it?

turns.prompt: Explain your phone is dying and ask to borrow their charger, softening it.

choices.ko: 미안한데 폰 배터리가 거의 다 돼서… 충전기 좀 빌려줄 수 있어?
choices.en: Sorry to ask, my phone's almost out of battery… could you lend me your charger?
choices.feedback: 미안한데 softens the request, and 배터리가 거의 다 됐어 is the natural way to say the battery is nearly empty.

choices.en: Hand over your charger, my phone's dying. (rude/demanding)
choices.feedback: 내놔 is a forceful command, and 폰 죽어 sounds translated rather than natural Korean.

choices.en: Do you have a charger? (abrupt, leaves out the actual request)
choices.feedback: This only checks whether a charger exists; it never asks to borrow it.

turns.ko: 아 그럼! 내 가방에 보조배터리도 있어. 이따 만날 때 줄게. 또 필요한 거 없어?
turns.en: Oh, of course! I've got a power bank in my bag too. I'll give it to you when we meet. Anything else you need?

turns.prompt: Ask them to also bring yesterday's class notes for you.

choices.ko: 오 진짜? 고마워!! 아 그리고 어제 수업 필기한 것도 좀 가져다줄 수 있어?
choices.en: Oh really? Thank you!! Could you also bring the notes you took in class yesterday?
choices.feedback: The thanks comes first, and -것도 좀 가져다줄 수 있어? adds a second request gently.

choices.en: Obviously you have to bring the notes too. (entitled tone)
choices.feedback: 당연히 and -아야지 treat your friend's help as an obligation.

choices.en: Don't you dare not bring the notes. (pushy)
choices.feedback: This is a prohibition, not a request, so it sounds pushy even between close friends.

turns.ko: ㅋㅋ 알겠어 필기도 챙겨 갈게. 진짜 다른 건 없고?
turns.en: Lol okay, I'll grab the notes too. You sure there's nothing else?

turns.prompt: Sheepishly ask to borrow a little cash for the bus since you left your card at home, and promise to pay it back.

choices.ko: 헐 진짜 미안한데… 나 카드를 집에 두고 와서 그런데 버스비로 이천 원만 빌려줄 수 있어? 이따 바로 갚을게
choices.en: I'm really sorry… I left my card at home. Could you lend me just 2,000 won for the bus? I'll pay you back right away.
choices.feedback: The reason, small amount, -줄 수 있어?, and 갚을게 make the request specific and considerate.

choices.en: Lend me some money, 10,000 won. (blunt, no softening)
choices.feedback: This jumps straight to a larger amount without explaining why or promising to repay it.

choices.en: You've got 10,000 won, right? Just give it to me. (demanding)
choices.feedback: 그냥 줘 asks your friend to give you money rather than lend it and sounds entitled.

turns.ko: 괜찮아 ㅋㅋ 이따 보내. 만날 때 다 챙겨 갈게!
turns.en: It's fine lol, send it later. I'll bring everything when we meet!

title: Politely asking a coworker a favor
situation: You have to leave the office early for an appointment, so you politely ask a coworker if they could pass a document to the team lead and cover a client call while you're out.
tip: In 존댓말, lead with 혹시 부탁 좀 드려도 될까요? to ask permission first, then 죄송하지만 + ~해 주실 수 있을까요? for the actual request. 혹시 and 좀 are the magic softeners.

turns.prompt: Politely ask permission to make a request before explaining.

choices.en: Could I possibly ask you a favor?
choices.feedback: 혹시 and -드려도 될까요? politely ask permission before you explain the favor.

choices.en: Do me a favor. (too blunt for a coworker)
choices.feedback: The request is grammatically polite, but the direct command 들어줘요 is too blunt for this coworker.

choices.en: I've got a favor, can you do it? (반말 — too casual at work)
choices.feedback: -줄 수 있어? is casual speech and mismatches the polite workplace conversation.

turns.prompt: Explain you have to leave early and ask if they could pass a document to the team lead.

choices.ko: 제가 오늘 좀 일찍 나가야 해서요. 죄송하지만 이 서류를 팀장님께 좀 전달해 주실 수 있을까요?
choices.en: I have to leave a bit early today. I'm sorry to ask, but could you pass this document to the team lead for me?
choices.feedback: The reason comes first, and 죄송하지만 plus -주실 수 있을까요? makes the workplace request considerate.

choices.ko: 저 먼저 갈게요. 이거 팀장님 주세요.
choices.en: I'm heading out first. Give this to the team lead. (curt, no softening)
choices.feedback: This announces your departure and gives an order without first asking whether your coworker can help.

choices.ko: 이 서류 좀 전달해. 나 가야 돼.
choices.en: Pass this document along. I gotta go. (반말, ordering)
choices.feedback: Both sentences are in casual speech and sound like an order in this workplace setting.

turns.ko: 아, 네. 그 정도는 괜찮아요. 언제까지 드리면 될까요?
turns.en: Oh, sure. I can do that. By when should I give it to them?

turns.prompt: Say before the 3 o'clock meeting is fine, and add a second small request to answer a call if a client phones.

choices.ko: 3시 회의 전까지만 팀장님께 전달해 주시면 돼요. 그리고 혹시 거래처에서 전화가 오면 대신 좀 받아 주실 수 있을까요?
choices.en: Just pass it to the team lead before the 3 o'clock meeting. And if a client calls, could you answer it for me?
choices.feedback: 전까지만 gives a clear deadline, and the second favor is introduced again with 혹시 and a polite question.

choices.en: Before the meeting. You answer the phone too. (반말, bossy)
choices.feedback: The clipped deadline and 네가 받아 sound bossy, and the casual speech is wrong for this coworker.

choices.en: Whenever. Just deal with the phone yourself. (dismissive)
choices.feedback: 아무 때나요 is vague, and 알아서 하세요 pushes responsibility onto the coworker dismissively.

turns.ko: 전화는 제가 받을게요. 그런데 거래처 건은 제가 내용을 잘 몰라서, 메모만 남겨 둬도 될까요?
turns.en: I'll take the call. But I don't really know the details of the client matter, so would it be okay if I just leave a note?

turns.prompt: Graciously accept their limit, make it easy for them, and thank them sincerely.

choices.ko: 그럼요, 메모만 남겨 주셔도 충분해요. 무리한 부탁을 드려서 죄송하고, 정말 감사합니다. 다음에 꼭 보답할게요!
choices.en: Of course, just a note is more than enough. Sorry for asking so much, and thank you so much. I'll definitely return the favor next time!
choices.feedback: This accepts the coworker's limit, lowers the burden, apologizes, and closes with sincere thanks.

choices.ko: 아니요, 꼭 통화하고 처리해 주셔야 돼요.
choices.en: No, you absolutely have to handle it on the call. (pushy, ignores their limit)
choices.feedback: 꼭 and -주셔야 돼요 ignore the coworker's reasonable limit and turn the favor into a demand.

choices.en: A note? That's kind of a problem. (ungracious)
choices.feedback: This rejects the help being offered without gratitude or an easier alternative.

turns.ko: 아니에요, 이 정도는 괜찮아요. 일 잘 보고 오세요.
turns.en: Not at all, this much is fine. Take care of your appointment.
